quests.sentence: No sooner had she spoken than she realised, with a sinking feeling, that her words had been misunderstood.
quests.hint: 'No sooner had she spoken' is an inverted past perfect - both events are past.
quests.explanation: 'No sooner had she spoken' is the inverted past perfect. 'Realised' and 'had been misunderstood' are also past.

quests.sentence: No sooner does she make a public statement than it is immediately analysed and debated in the media.
quests.hint: 'Does she make' is inverted present - describing what always happens now.
quests.explanation: 'Does she make' is the inverted present simple in a 'no sooner...than' pattern for a current habit.

quests.sentence: No sooner will she have spoken than the debate about the meaning of her words will begin in earnest.
quests.hint: 'Will have spoken' and 'will begin' are both future.
quests.explanation: 'Will have spoken' is the future perfect; 'will begin' is the future simple. Both are future events.

quests.sentence: The chairman had barely finished his carefully prepared opening remarks when the first strong objection was raised.
quests.hint: 'Had barely finished' and 'was raised' are past - both completed past events.
quests.explanation: 'Had barely finished' is the past perfect. 'Was raised' is the past simple passive. Both are past.

quests.sentence: The chairman has barely finished one set of remarks when questions immediately begin to pour in from the floor.
quests.hint: 'Has barely finished' and 'begin' are present - this describes what always happens now.
quests.explanation: 'Has barely finished' is the present perfect in a pattern describing a current recurring situation.

quests.sentence: The chairman will barely have finished his remarks when the full and vigorous debate begins in earnest.
quests.hint: 'Will barely have finished' and 'begins' are both future.
quests.explanation: 'Will barely have finished' is the future perfect. The debate is a future event that follows almost immediately.

quests.sentence: It was only after the project had been fully delivered that its true and total cost became entirely apparent.
quests.hint: 'It was only after' - the project is delivered (past); the cost becoming apparent is also past.
quests.explanation: 'Was' and 'had been delivered' and 'became' are all past forms. The realisation follows delivery, both past.

quests.sentence: It is only after a major project is completed that its real long-term value becomes fully and properly apparent.
quests.hint: 'Is' and 'is completed' and 'becomes' are present - this is a general truth.
quests.explanation: 'Is' and 'becomes' are present simple forms in a zero conditional expressing a general present truth.

quests.sentence: It will only be after the full and independent audit has concluded that the real savings will be known.
quests.hint: 'Will only be' and 'will be known' are future - the audit hasn't finished yet.
quests.explanation: 'Will only be' and 'will be known' are future simple forms. The audit is a future event.

quests.sentence: Such was the extraordinary scale of the disruption that international aid and support arrived within hours.
quests.hint: 'Such was' is an inverted past - the disruption has already occurred.
quests.explanation: 'Such was' is an inverted past simple. The sentence describes the past scale of a completed disruption.

quests.sentence: Such is the overwhelming scale of the ongoing crisis that organisations from across the world are mobilising.
quests.hint: 'Such is' is an inverted present - describing the current scale of the crisis.
quests.explanation: 'Such is' is the inverted present simple. The sentence describes the current, ongoing scale of a crisis.

quests.sentence: Such will be the scale of the coming transformation that no single country will manage it alone.
quests.hint: 'Such will be' is an inverted future - the transformation is ahead.
quests.explanation: 'Such will be' is the inverted future simple. The sentence makes a prediction about the scale of future change.

quests.sentence: Not since the severe disruptions of the 1970s had global financial markets experienced such extreme and sustained volatility.
quests.hint: 'Not since the 1970s had experienced' is the inverted past perfect - a historically unprecedented past event.
quests.explanation: 'Not since... had experienced' is the inverted past perfect. The sentence compares a past event to a historical precedent.

quests.sentence: Not since the financial crisis of 2008 has the global economy faced a period of such deep and prolonged uncertainty.
quests.hint: 'Has faced' is the present perfect with 'not since' - from 2008 up to now.
quests.explanation: 'Not since 2008 has faced' is the inverted present perfect. The sentence spans from a past point to the present.

quests.sentence: Not for many decades to come will the markets return to the kind of stability the world once knew.
quests.hint: 'Will the markets return' is an inverted future - stability is far ahead.
quests.explanation: 'Not for many decades will return' is the inverted future simple. The sentence predicts a distant future outcome.

quests.sentence: Little did she know, at that critical moment, that the decision she was making would change the course of history.
quests.hint: 'Little did she know' is an inverted past - the decision has already been made.
quests.explanation: 'Little did she know' is the inverted past simple. 'Was making' and 'would change' are also past forms.

quests.sentence: Little does she know that the research she is currently pursuing will one day be celebrated worldwide.
quests.hint: 'Little does she know' is inverted present - she is currently unaware.
quests.explanation: 'Little does she know' is the inverted present simple. 'Is pursuing' is the present continuous.

quests.sentence: Little will she realise, at the very moment of making the decision, what its far-reaching consequences will be.
quests.hint: 'Little will she realise' is an inverted future - the realisation is ahead.
quests.explanation: 'Little will she realise' is the inverted future simple. The decision and its consequences are future events.

quests.sentence: Scarcely had the full board meeting convened when the most contentious issue of all was immediately raised.
quests.hint: 'Scarcely had the meeting convened' is an inverted past perfect - the meeting is past.
quests.explanation: 'Scarcely had convened' is the inverted past perfect. 'Was raised' is the past simple passive. Both are past.

quests.sentence: Scarcely does a board meeting pass without at least one contentious and difficult disagreement arising.
quests.hint: 'Scarcely does pass' is inverted present - describing what always happens in the present.
quests.explanation: 'Scarcely does pass' is the inverted present simple in a pattern describing a current regular pattern.

quests.sentence: Scarcely will a day go by, once the process begins, without some significant new development emerging.
quests.hint: 'Will a day go by' is inverted future - the process hasn't started yet.
quests.explanation: 'Scarcely will go by' is the inverted future simple. 'Once the process begins' is a future condition.

quests.sentence: Rarely had the international scientific community been divided so deeply on a question so fundamentally important.
quests.hint: 'Rarely had been divided' is an inverted past perfect - a historically unusual past state.
quests.explanation: 'Rarely had been divided' is the inverted past perfect passive. The sentence describes an unusual past situation.

quests.sentence: Rarely is there a scientific question on which leading researchers agree as broadly and consistently as this one.
quests.hint: 'Rarely is there' is an inverted present - describing an unusual current situation.
quests.explanation: 'Rarely is there' is the inverted present simple existential. The sentence describes an unusual current consensus.

quests.sentence: Rarely will an international opportunity of this bilateral significance and potential present itself again.
quests.hint: 'Rarely will present' is an inverted future - predicting a rare future event.
quests.explanation: 'Rarely will present' is the inverted future simple. The sentence predicts the future rarity of such an opportunity.

quests.sentence: Only when all the relevant facts had finally been laid out before them did the full committee reach its considered conclusion.
quests.hint: 'Only when all facts had been laid out did reach' - both are past.
quests.explanation: 'Had been laid out' is the past perfect passive. 'Did reach' is the inverted past simple. Both are past.

quests.sentence: Only when all the available evidence has been thoroughly reviewed does the committee feel confident to make a recommendation.
quests.hint: 'Has been reviewed' and 'does feel' are present - this is the current procedure.
quests.explanation: 'Has been reviewed' is the present perfect passive. 'Does feel' is the inverted present simple.

quests.sentence: Only when all the relevant data has been properly gathered and verified will investigators be able to draw firm conclusions.
quests.hint: 'Will investigators be able' is inverted future - the data gathering is still ahead.
quests.explanation: 'Will be able to draw' is the future modal. 'Only when the data has been gathered' is a future condition.

quests.sentence: So profound and far-reaching was the impact of the discovery that it fundamentally reshaped the entire discipline.
quests.hint: 'So profound was' is an inverted past - the reshaping has already occurred.
quests.explanation: 'So profound was' is the inverted past simple. 'Reshaped' is the simple past. Both describe completed past events.

quests.sentence: So complex is the existing regulatory framework that most ordinary citizens are largely unfamiliar with their rights.
quests.hint: 'So complex is' is an inverted present - describing the current state of affairs.
quests.explanation: 'So complex is' is the inverted present simple. The sentence describes a current ongoing reality.

quests.sentence: So comprehensive will the new regulations be that businesses will require considerable time and expert guidance to comply.
quests.hint: 'So comprehensive will be' is an inverted future - the regulations don't exist yet.
quests.explanation: 'So comprehensive will be' is the inverted future simple. The sentence makes a prediction about future regulations.
